newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KAL eyes for global cargo alliance.
newsitem.headline: KAL eyes for global cargo alliance.

text.p: Korean Air Ltd (KAL) is talking to "four or five" airlines about a global cargo alliance, KAL's cargo vice-president and general manager, Ji Young Lee told Reuters.
He declined to identify the potential partners but added in an interview that one of them could be an existing alliance partner.
Lee said the world-wide cargo alliance under study includes pooling aircraft, sharing and selling cargo space with the aim of "increasing market domination".
"We will be able to cover the whole world via this network to compete against our real competitors who are the integrators," Lee added.
"We are in the early stages of talks but many details still have to be worked out and that's all I can say," he said.
Integrators include companies such as Federal Express Corp, DHL Worldwide Express and United Parcel Service of America who offer time-definite deliveries and control the whole shipment process.

KAL already operates joint ventures on key international routes with Air France, Deutsche Lufthansa, Garuda Indonesia, Malaysia Airline System Bhd, Alitalia, British Airways Plc Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Philippine Airlines and Japan Airlines Ltd.

He described the cargo alliance as a similar concept to the proposed British Airways/American Airlines transatlantic alliance which has provoked controversy about market domination. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
